summary: Describes how the Layer Two Tunneling Protocol (L2TP) can use an ATM network, via AAL5, as its underlying network connection instead of IP. It covers using ATM signalling to set up the connection between a dial-up server and a network access server.

plainLanguage.summary: L2TP usually travels over internet connections. This document shows how to run it over ATM instead, which is another kind of network.

subtitle: How to run L2TP tunnels over an ATM virtual circuit using AAL5, including the two encapsulations and SVC signalling.

tldr.problem: L2TP only needs a packet-oriented point-to-point link underneath it, but it does not say how to get one from an ATM network.
tldr.mechanism: An AAL5 virtual circuit carries one L2TP packet per AAL5 PDU, either behind an LLC/SNAP header or as the bare payload, and switched circuits are set up with Q.2931 signalling that names the encapsulation.
tldr.outcome: Implementations must support LLC encapsulation on permanent circuits, and may support the other options.

today: RFC 3355 is a Proposed Standard published in August 2002. The unit metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: L2TP and ATM
sections.content:
PPP is often used on the link between a personal computer with a dial modem and a network service provider. L2TP (RFC 2661) lets a dial-up server, the L2TP Access Concentrator (LAC), extend that PPP connection through a tunnel to a remote L2TP Network Server (LNS).

L2TP requires only that the tunnel media provide packet oriented point-to-point connectivity. An ATM network with AAL5 offers such a connection, and RFC 3355 supplements RFC 2661 with the details for using AAL5 between a LAC and an LNS. It supports ATM UNI Signaling Version 4.0 or Version 3.1.
sections.plainLanguage: L2TP needs a pipe to send its messages through. This document says how to use an ATM connection as that pipe.

sections.title: The AAL5 Service Interface
sections.content:
L2TP treats the AAL5 layer as a bit-synchronous point-to-point link, and the L2TP link corresponds to an AAL5 virtual circuit. The circuit MUST be full-duplex and point to point, and MAY be dedicated (a permanent circuit set up by provisioning) or switched (set up on demand). AAL5 message mode in non-assured operation, without the corrupted delivery option, MUST be used.

Each L2TP PDU MUST travel in a single AAL5 PDU, so the AAL5 MTU constrains the MTU of the tunnel and of every PPP connection inside it. An implementation MUST support a PPP MRU of at least 1500 bytes, SHOULD use a larger MTU, and it is RECOMMENDED to support an IP packet of at least 9180 bytes in the PPP PDU.

For quality of service, an implementation MAY use more than one AAL5 connection between LAC and LNS. Inverse multiplexing a tunnel across several circuits is left for further study. L2TP imposes no limits on transmission rate or ATM traffic descriptors, which may be agreed between the parties for a permanent circuit or requested at setup for a switched one.
sections.plainLanguage: The pipe must carry traffic both ways, and each tunnel message has to fit in one piece. You should be able to send at least a 1500 byte packet, and more is better.

sections.title: Choosing an Encapsulation
sections.content:
The RFC builds on RFC 2684. L2TP PDUs go in the payload of AAL5 CPCS PDUs and the SSCS is empty. RFC 2684 offers two ways to identify the payload protocol: VC-based multiplexing, where both ends agree on the protocol for the circuit, and LLC encapsulation, where each PDU carries an IEEE 802.2 LLC header.

An implementation:

  • MUST support LLC encapsulated L2TP on permanent circuits (PVCs).
  • MAY support LLC encapsulated L2TP on switched circuits (SVCs).
  • MAY support VC-multiplexed L2TP on PVCs or SVCs.

On a PVC the endpoints must be configured to use one of the two methods. An implementation connecting through a Frame Relay/ATM FRF.8 interworking unit MUST use LLC encapsulation.
sections.plainLanguage: There are two ways to label the envelopes: write the label on every envelope, or agree in advance that this pipe only carries one kind. Everyone has to be able to do the first way.

sections.title: LLC and VC-Multiplexed Formats
sections.content:
With LLC encapsulation, the AAL5 payload starts with an LLC header: destination and source SAP of 0xAA and a frame type of Unnumbered Information, 0x03. That header says an IEEE 802.1a SNAP header follows. The SNAP header holds the three-octet OUI 0x00-00-5E, which identifies IANA, and a two-octet PID of 0x0007, which identifies L2TP. The L2TP PDU comes next.

With VC-multiplexed encapsulation, sometimes called Null encapsulation, the L2TP PDU is the AAL5 payload with no LLC header.

Either way the AAL5 CPCS-PDU has the same shape: the payload (up to 2^16 - 1 octets), a PAD of 0 to 47 octets that makes the trailer end at the cell boundary, and a trailer with CPCS-UU (1 octet, may be set to any value), CPI (1 octet, coded 0x00 when only 64-bit alignment is used), Length (2 octets, maximum 65535) and CRC (4 octets, computed over the whole CPCS-PDU except the CRC). A Length of 0x00 MAY be used for the abort function. The endpoints may also be provisioned to send other LLC-encapsulated protocols on the same circuit.
sections.plainLanguage: The LLC way puts a short note on the front that says this is L2TP. The other way skips the note. Both end with the same fixed trailer that checks nothing got scrambled.

sections.title: Setting Up and Tearing Down SVCs
sections.content:
A switched circuit can be started by the LAC or the LNS, and an implementation that supports SVCs MUST be able to both originate and respond to setup requests. It MUST use the Q.2931 Annex C procedure, with the Broadband Lower Layer Information (B-LLI) information element naming the encapsulation. The caller requests VC-multiplexed, LLC encapsulated or both in the SETUP message. If it offers both, the two B-LLI elements go in a Broadband Repeat Indicator in order of preference.

An implementation MUST accept an incoming call that offers LLC encapsulated L2TP, and a called peer MUST reject a request that offers only an encapsulation it does not support. If both are offered and accepted, the called peer puts exactly one B-LLI in the Connect message.

For LLC calls, the layer 2 protocol field selects LAN Logical Link Control (ISO/IEC8802-2). For VC-multiplexed calls it selects no layer 2 protocol and the layer 3 field selects ISO/IEC TR 9577, with the user information encoded as 0B 80 00 00 5E 00 07.

If an SVC tunnel is reset per section 4.1 of RFC 2661, both ends MUST clear it and sessions end. After a failed setup, the caller MAY treat the peer as unreachable until told otherwise, and either end MAY clear an SVC with no active sessions. When an SVC is cleared, an implementation SHALL tear down the tunnel and return the control connection to idle.
sections.plainLanguage: When making a call on demand, the caller says which envelope style it wants. The other side says yes to one or no thanks. If the call is dropped, the tunnel is dropped too.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The L2TP base specification (RFC 2661) covers basic security issues. The RFC adds that an L2TP over AAL5 tunnel could be compromised by an attack on the ATM transport network itself. The ATM Forum has published a security framework and a security specification, and applications needing protection against threats to an ATM switching network are encouraged to use authentication headers, encrypted payloads, or the ATM-layer security services of the ATM Forum specification.
sections.plainLanguage: The tunnel is only as safe as the pipe it runs in, so people who worry about snoopers should add locks of their own.
